ops.note: Both were weighed against the existing flock generation protocol before any change, and the protocol's shape was left intact — no new lock ordering, no redesign. Prune uses a non-blocking exclusive acquire specifically because a foreground dispatch holds EX to process exit, so a blocking acquire would stall --ps for a whole codex run; unlink-while-held was reasoned through (the flock rides the open descriptor, and the residual micro-window fails loud rather than deleting a live run). The --await guard is a pure path predicate that dies before any fd is opened, so lock ordering is unchanged.
